claims.text: A machine-learning approach that tailors thermomechanical processing conditions can overcome the strength–ductility trade-off.
Engineering fine multiphase microstructures with coherent interfaces can reduce the strength–ductility trade-off in metallic structural alloys.
Standard processing produces high strength but low ductility in the target alloys.
Incoherent interfaces and limited phase control cause the low ductility of conventionally processed structural alloys.
A machine-learning model can systematically correlate temperature, deformation, and annealing time with multiphase structures and coherent precipitates.
Such a machine-learning model can identify optimal processing pathways.
The proposed samples will be evaluated under ambient and elevated-temperature conditions while processing parameters are varied according to machine-learning recommendations.
The desired structural mediator is a fine multiphase microstructure containing coherent precipitates or well-arranged phase boundaries.
The relevant multiphase structure may be an ordered/disordered mixture such as fcc/B2 or B2/BCC.
The engineered phase features block dislocations and thereby increase strength.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that could initiate premature cracks.
Machine-learning-optimized processing conditions cause controlled formation of coherent interfaces and fine nanoprecipitates.
The engineered microstructure can accommodate local transformations that enhance ductility.
The optimized alloy will have greater ductility without a loss of yield strength relative to a conventionally processed counterpart.
The optimized alloy may achieve strength above 2 GPa together with ductility above 10%.
Traditional trial-and-error processing typically enhances strength at the expense of ductility.
Success depends on the alloy's ability to form beneficial multiphase microstructures and on the accuracy and training data of the machine-learning model.
The degree of simultaneous strength and ductility improvement will vary with alloy system and processing window.
